description: Prompt for Copilot CLI to fix the problems of one ESLint rule, plus settings per rule. 'fixedInstructions' always come first and cannot be edited by the user; 'prompt' is the default of the editable instructions. Lines are joined with a space. {ruleId} is replaced by the rule, {messageFile} by the file for the commit message and {problemsFile} by the file with the problems of the rule. Per rule in 'rules' (rule id -> object): 'instructions' (list of lines, shown as separate lines in the editable instructions) are added after 'prompt' under a heading, and 'defaultMode' (interactive, plan or autopilot; interactive when absent) is the preselected Copilot mode. 'defaultModels' are the models offered first in the model question (models used before in the project are appended after them); another question lists all models of Copilot. Keep everything free of double quotes, backticks and shell characters (single quotes are fine): the prompt is passed through a shell inside double quotes.
fixedInstructions: The problems to fix are listed in the file {problemsFile}; read it while you plan. Do not run the check command while planning, as plan mode blocks it. The task is done when this command returns 0: npx uselab-linting check '{ruleId}'. Run it once you start implementing. When you are done, write a one-line commit message that describes the fix to the file {messageFile}, then tell me to type /exit to return.
prompt: Fix only the ESLint problems of the rule {ruleId} in this project. Do not change code for other eslint rules.

Fix the root cause. Do not take shortcuts: do not disable the rule, add eslint-disable-next-line comments, change the ESLint config or ignores, use ts-ignore or any or type assertions to silence the error without my permission.
If you create new files or move files make sure they are tracked by Git.

instructions: Replace any with the real type, a generic, or unknown with a type guard.
Prefer types that already exist in the project or its dependencies over new ones.
Move the file into app/, features/ or support/ inside the src folder. Decide where it goes with this checklist, first match wins:
1. Entry or wiring file (main.ts, composition of features, routes): put it in app/.
2. It uses or knows about one business feature: put it in features/ inside the folder of that feature.
3. It is used by two or more features and has no business knowledge: put it in support/.
4. It is used by two or more features but is business specific: put it in the feature that owns the concept, and let app/ wire the features together. Do not import one feature from another.
5. Still unsure: stop and ask me where it belongs.
Update every import of the moved file so nothing breaks.
Booleans and numbers are usually better in a single object parameter than as separate parameters.
A single object parameter with properties for each boolean or number are better in many cases. It is more readable.
Allowed imports: app/ may import app/, features and support/; a feature may import itself and support/; support/ may import only support/.
Resolve a violation with this checklist, first match wins:
1. Generic code with no business knowledge that sits in a feature or app/ and is needed elsewhere: move it to support/.

2. Feature A imports feature B: do not move the import. Keep the logic in B, make A receive what it needs as a function, callback or data parameter typed in A or in support/, and call B and pass the result to A in app/.
3. support/ imports a feature or app/: invert the dependency. Let support/ define the type or interface and let the feature or app/ pass in the implementation.
4. A feature imports app/: move the shared code to support/, or pass it in from app/.
5. None of these fit, for example because A cannot work without B concepts: stop and ask me.
Do not use hoisting to fix this issue.
